sentences.text: Ms. Monica Mishra, learned counsel for the appellant.
Ms. Anjali Gyanani, learned GA for respondent/State.
Heard on I.A.No.13668/2025, an application under Section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C. on behalf of sole appellant - Rakesh for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

2. This criminal appeal assails the judgment dated 27.08.2021 passed by Additional Sessions Judge,
Chachoda District Guna, M.P. in ST No.77/2016; whereby, present appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under :-
 Section Imprisonment Fine  342 of IPC 6 Months R.I. Rs.1,000/- with defa 376 (2)(n) of IPC 10 years R.I. Rs.5,000/- with default stipulations 376 (d) of IPC 20 years R.I.
Rs.10,000/- with default stipulations 3.

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge,
Chachoda District Guna, M.P.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is the submission of counsel for present appellant that the trial Court erred in convicting and awarding jail sentence to appellant.
It is the submission of counsel for the appellant that prosecutrix was at the cusp of attaining majority, however, as per prosecution, age of prosecutrix was around 13 years.

Medical report belies the allegations because Dr. Jyoti Yadav (PW-7) categorically admits that there was no injury over her person including private parts and looking to her medical condition,
qua the allegations, injuries were ought to be there but in absence of any injury, and 2 CRA-5429-2021 medical report given by doctor, it is a case of false implication.
Even the witnesses who were alleged eyewitnesses (after crime being committed) did not support the story of prosecution and declared hostile.
Because of previous enmity as reflected in admission of witness- Dropadi Bai (PW- 1) false allegations were leveled.
Appellant has already suffered four years and five months of incarceration as pre and post trial confinement.
Final hearing of the appeal shall take some time and he has a good case on merits.

sentences.text: He undertakes to abide by all terms and conditions as imposed by this Court.
Thus, appellant be granted benefit of suspension of sentence.
4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of application.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and record perused.
6.

Considering the submissions advanced by counsel for the parties, but without commenting on the merits of the case, I.A.No.13668/2025 filed on behalf of sole appellant - Rakesh stands allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of present appellant shall remain suspended during pendency of the present appeal and he shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court concerned and the deposit of fine amount is deferred so that appellant may deposit the same if the appeal is dismissed on merits.
The appellant is directed to appear before the Registry of this Court first on 28.11.2025 and on other subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf.

7. Present appellant shall not be a source of embarrassment and 3 CRA-5429-2021 harassment to the complainant/victim side in any manner; shall not move in their vicinity otherwise, benefit of bail given today by way of suspension of sentence shall be withdrawn immediately.
8. Accordingly, the application stands disposed of.

9. Observations on facts, if any, are only for the purpose of deciding the instant I.A. and shall have no bearing on the merits of the appeal.
10.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for information and necessary compliance.

(ANAND PATHAK) (PUSHPENDR  JUDGE JUD  Ashish*
